title: Blood orange curd tart
subtitle: a crisp pastry case filled with set blood orange curd
excerpt: Blood orange curd tart uses the same method as a lemon curd tart but with fresh blood oranges, which have a deeper, more complex citrus flavour and a vivid pink-red juice. The curd is made on the hob then poured into a blind-baked pastry case and left to set. It is sharper and less sweet than a lemon tart, so the filling is generous with the citrus.
sourceNotes: Blood orange curd tart, a variation on the classic French lemon tart (tarte au citron). Blood orange curd method from contemporary British patisserie.

glossaryTerms.definition: A cooked mixture of citrus juice, eggs, butter, and sugar that sets to a thick, spreadable consistency on cooling. The egg yolks and butter give it a smooth, creamy texture.
Baking a pastry case without its filling, to prevent it becoming soggy once the wet filling is added. The case is lined with parchment and weighted with baking beans.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The tart keeps refrigerated for up to 3 days. The filling may darken slightly but the flavour is unchanged.

Rub the cold butter into the flour and icing sugar to fine crumbs. Stir in the egg yolk and enough cold water (about 2 tablespoons) to bring the pastry together. Chill for 30 minutes, then roll out and line a 23 cm loose-bottomed tart tin. Refrigerate for a further 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan. Blind-bake for 15 minutes, then remove the beans and bake for 8 to 10 more minutes until the base is golden and completely dry. Cool fully.

Whisk together the blood orange juice, zest, caster sugar, whole eggs, and egg yolks in a medium heavy-based saucepan. Cook over a low-medium heat, stirring constantly, for 8 to 10 minutes until the mixture thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon. Do not let it boil.
Remove from the heat and stir in the butter a piece at a time until fully melted and incorporated. Strain through a fine sieve into a jug.
Pour immediately into the cooled pastry case. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours until the curd is firmly set. Serve at room temperature with crème fraîche.

attrs.problem: Curd scrambled with lumps of cooked egg
attrs.avoid: Avoid too high a heat; scrambled egg curd cannot be recovered.
attrs.fix: Keep the heat low and stir constantly. If you see the mixture beginning to curdle at the edges, remove from the heat immediately and strain.

attrs.problem: Curd too thin and does not set in the tart
attrs.avoid: Avoid removing from the heat too early; the curd must coat the spoon visibly before pouring.
attrs.fix: Return to a very low heat and cook for a further 2 to 3 minutes until thickened.
